item.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 David Vesterlund
This paper studies how much Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) work can be avoided while preserving optimization quality in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). Using exact statevector simulation of QAOA on six graph optimization problems across seven graph families, three baselines are compared: a naive QPU-centric workflow with 30 quantum evaluations, a best-practice workflow that separates classical parameter optimization from a single QPU evaluation, and a classical-only solver. Six QPUminimization strategies are evaluated: preprocessing, pretraining, surrogate modeling, adaptive stopping, adaptive shots, and measurement reuse.
